title: Applied anatomy: the lumbar spine and spinal cord for lumbar puncture

related.why: Spinal cord injury: the same cord levels applied to trauma

brief.role: Core surgical trainee on the ward
brief.scenario: Fiona Lamont, 42, has fever, headache and neck stiffness. The medical team suspect meningitis and plan a lumbar puncture.
brief.task: Answer the examiner's questions on the vertebral column and spinal cord and relate them to a safe lumbar puncture.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Vertebra, where the cord ends, which gap, what the needle passes, and when not to do it.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Reciting layers while missing that a drowsy patient with focal signs must not have a lumbar puncture yet.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: "The cord ends at about L1–L2 in adults, so I'd go below it at L3–L4 or L4–L5."

flow: Where the cord and sac end

grid.label: Lumbar vertebra
grid.fail: Cannot name the parts of a lumbar vertebra.
grid.pass: Body, pedicles, laminae, transverse and spinous processes, articular facets, vertebral foramen; laminae joined by ligamentum flavum.
grid.high: Lumbar spinous processes are broad and near-horizontal, so the needle aims slightly cephalad; flexion opens the interlaminar gap.

grid.label: Where the cord and sac end
grid.fail: Says the cord ends at L4 or does not know.
grid.pass: Conus medullaris at about L1–L2 in adults; dural sac to S2; cauda equina and filum terminale below the conus.
grid.high: Knows the range: on MRI the conus lies from mid T12 to upper L3; in infants it can lie at L2–L3.

grid.label: Choose the level
grid.pass: L3–L4 or L4–L5, below the conus. The line joining the iliac crests crosses about L4.
grid.high: Knows the crest line is only at L4 in about two-thirds of adults and palpation errs, so stays at or below it.

grid.label: Layers the needle passes
grid.fail: Omits ligamentum flavum or puts the epidural space inside the dura.
grid.pass: Skin, fat, supraspinous and interspinous ligaments, ligamentum flavum, epidural space, dura, arachnoid, subarachnoid space.
grid.high: Epidural space holds fat and the internal vertebral venous plexus; resistance lost after the flavum; paramedian route skips the midline ligaments.

grid.label: Position
grid.fail: Places her with the back rotated or unflexed.
grid.pass: Lateral with hips, knees and neck flexed, back at the bed edge, shoulders and hips vertical; or sitting.
grid.high: Measures opening pressure lying lateral, not sitting.

grid.label: When not to do it
grid.fail: Proceeds in a patient with focal signs or falling GCS without imaging.
grid.pass: No LP with spreading purpura, infection at the site, signs of raised pressure (focal signs, abnormal pupils, GCS 9 or less, falling GCS).
grid.high: Does not image routinely; if LP is unsafe, takes blood cultures and gives antibiotics without waiting; corrects bleeding risk first.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: Name the parts of a typical lumbar vertebra.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: The body and the spine at the back.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: Where does the spinal cord end?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Any lumbar gap, L1–L2 is easiest to feel.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: What does the needle pass through?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Skin, muscle, dura, then the epidural space and CSF.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: She is sitting slumped and twisted to one side.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: That's fine, I'll just go in.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: She now has a GCS of 9 and a dilated pupil.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I'd still do the LP first to get the diagnosis.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Name the parts of a typical lumbar vertebra.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Body, pedicles, laminae, transverse and spinous processes, the articular facets and the vertebral foramen. Adjacent laminae are joined by ligamentum flavum.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: The conus is at about L1–L2 in adults. The dural sac goes on to S2, containing the cauda equina.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: L3–L4 or L4–L5, below the conus. The line between the iliac crests crosses about L4.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: What does the needle pass through?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Skin, fat, supraspinous ligament, interspinous ligament, ligamentum flavum, epidural space, dura and arachnoid, into the subarachnoid space.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: On her side, hips, knees and neck flexed, back at the edge of the bed, shoulders and hips vertical.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: When would you not do it?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Spreading purpura, infection at the site, or signs of raised pressure: new focal signs, abnormal pupils, GCS 9 or less or a falling GCS.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Anything about the lumbar spinous processes?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: They're broad and nearly horizontal, so I aim slightly towards the head. Flexion opens the gap between the laminae.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Is L1–L2 always safe for the cord?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: No. On MRI the conus ranges from mid T12 to upper L3, and in infants it can lie at L2–L3.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: How reliable is the crest line?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: It's at L4 in only about two-thirds of adults, and palpation errs. I stay at or below it.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: What lies in the epidural space?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Fat and the internal vertebral venous plexus. I feel the loss of resistance after the flavum. A paramedian approach avoids the midline ligaments.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I'd measure opening pressure with her lying on her side, not sitting.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: She is drowsy with a GCS of 12. Should she be scanned first?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: NICE advises against routine imaging, but a falling GCS is a sign of raised pressure, so no LP now. I'd take blood cultures and give antibiotics without waiting, and correct any bleeding risk before any later LP.

failures.move: Proceeding with focal signs, abnormal pupils or a falling GCS.
failures.consequence: Risks coning; antibiotics are delayed while waiting.
The needle may reach the conus in adults whose cord ends low.
Cannot explain the loss of resistance or the epidural space.
No anatomical basis for choosing a safe level.

recovery.line: Outside in: skin, ligaments back to front, flavum, epidural space, dura, arachnoid, CSF.
Signs of raised pressure: no LP now, antibiotics without waiting.

knowledge.fact: Conus at about L1–L2 in adults (MRI range mid T12 to upper L3).
Under 2 years the conus can lie at L2–L3.
Supracristal line at L4 in 69% of adults on CT.
Needle path: supraspinous, interspinous, flavum, epidural space (fat, venous plexus), dura, arachnoid.
No LP with spreading purpura, site infection, or signs of raised pressure: focal signs, abnormal pupils, GCS 9 or less, falling GCS.

recall.think: Cord injury from too high a level; coning if pressure is raised.
do: Enter at or below the crest line
recall.trap: The crest line is not always L4.
recall.finish: Sample CSF; if LP unsafe, antibiotics without delay.

partner.opening: Name the parts of a typical lumbar vertebra.

reveals.trigger: After the parts of the vertebra
reveals.finding: Ask: on a midline sagittal MRI of an adult lumbar spine, the spinal cord tapers to a point and only nerve roots continue below it within the dural sac. At what vertebral level does the cord usually end, and where does the sac end?

reveals.trigger: Candidate asks about her conscious level and neurology
reveals.finding: GCS 14, pupils equal and reactive, no focal signs, no rash, no anticoagulants, platelets normal.

reveals.trigger: Candidate asks how she is positioned
reveals.finding: She is sitting slumped and rotated to the left.

push.question: Where does the cord end?
push.expect: About L1–L2 in adults; sac to S2.

push.question: Which level, and how do you find it?
push.expect: L3–L4 or L4–L5; crest line at about L4.

push.question: What does the needle pass through?
push.expect: Supraspinous, interspinous, flavum, epidural space, dura, arachnoid.

push.question: When would you not do it?
push.expect: Spreading purpura, site infection, signs of raised pressure.

curveballs.prompt: Her GCS falls to 12 and her right pupil is sluggish.
curveballs.safeAnswer: No LP. Blood cultures and antibiotics now; imaging and senior review.

curveballs.prompt: Should everyone have a CT head before LP?
curveballs.safeAnswer: No. Only with features of raised pressure or a possible space-occupying lesion.

curveballs.prompt: Where is the tip of the cord in a newborn?
curveballs.safeAnswer: It can lie lower, at L2–L3, so a low interspace is used.
